topic: What if Itachi never planted Shisui's Kotoamatsukami crow in Naruto, leaving Kabuto's Edo Tensei hold on Itachi unbroken
title: What If Itachi Never Put The Crow In Naruto?
description:
What if Itachi never planted Shisui's Kotoamatsukami crow inside Naruto during the crow scene? Without it, Kabuto keeps Itachi as a puppet in chapter 549, Izanami never happens, and Sasuke never gets the conversation that turned him away from Konoha. We follow the chain one step at a time and land on a twist about what the crow was really for.

1:28 A Promise Inside A Bird
4:01 Kabuto's Perfect Puppet
6:38 Brothers Without Words
9:10 The Net That Missed
11:45 The Verdict

Was the crow Itachi's plan for Sasuke or his gift to Naruto?
comment: Was Itachi's crow always meant for Sasuke, or did Itachi secretly know it would end up freeing himself? Pick one.

lines.text: Itachi's smartest move came after he was gone, and it was one crow slipped into Naruto.

lines.text: One bird, one promise, planted in Naruto. I think that crow is the most important object in Itachi's whole plan.

lines.text: The crow was never aimed at Kabuto. Itachi had somebody else in mind.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: So who was it really built to stop? And why does that make this timeline so much darker?

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: Start with the bird itself, because Itachi did not choose it by accident, and neither did the eye inside it.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: Every piece of his life is a move made three steps ahead, and this crow is the longest of them.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: Because the man who planned that crow also planned how his brother would hate him for years.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: This isn't a power-scaling argument. It's a plan argument, and I think Itachi wins plan arguments against almost anyone.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: But a beautiful scene is exactly where a plan can hide its weakest joint.

shot.fallback: dark haired ninja with red eyes and a black crow, night sky

lines.text: I want to be fair to the canon version here, because it's already a beautiful scene.

lines.text: Except the bird only matters if you understand whose eye is inside it...

lines.text: Shisui Uchiha owned a technique called Kotoamatsukami, a genjutsu that bends someone's will without them ever feeling it.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Shisui entrusted his remaining eye to Itachi before he died.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Danzo did take the other one. He carried Shisui's eye in his bandaged socket for years.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Itachi, meanwhile, put the surviving eye somewhere nobody would think to look: inside a crow.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Now jump to the crow scene. Naruto is walking alone when a swarm of crows closes around him.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: It's an Itachi clone, and Naruto is trapped in a genjutsu before he can even draw a weapon.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: The clone asks one thing. If Sasuke ever turns on Konoha, what will you do?

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Naruto doesn't dodge it. He says he'll stop Sasuke, but he will not kill him.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: That answer is the whole reason the crow goes into him. Itachi was not testing strength. He was testing loyalty.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Then a single crow flies into Naruto's mouth, and Naruto forgets it was ever there.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: My read is that Itachi spent years shaping how the next generation would answer exactly that question.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Here is the detail most people forget. The eye was programmed for whoever held Itachi's Mangekyo Sharingan.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Itachi expected that to be Sasuke, since Sasuke would need those eyes once his own failed him.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: The plan was simple: if Sasuke ever marched on Konoha with Itachi's eyes, Kotoamatsukami would bend him to protect it.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: It could only fire about once in ten years, so Itachi built one shot and gave it a patient hiding place.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: People say the crow ended up doing something completely different, so it proves nothing about the plan. Fair.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: But that's the point. A safety net can catch the wrong person and still save everything.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: That's what I keep coming back to. Itachi trusted Naruto with a secret Naruto couldn't open.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Naruto doesn't even know the crow exists. The man who carries the plan isn't allowed to read it.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Think about how much faith that takes. He picks the one person who refuses to stop calling Sasuke his friend.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Itachi could have trusted Sasuke to find the right path alone. He didn't. He built a backup, then a backup for the backup.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Itachi bets on a boy who barely knows him, because that boy is the only one who won't give up on Sasuke.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Kishimoto uses this scene to show the Uchiha plan wasn't only about eyes. It was about people.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: He walks into the war with a stranger's spell tucked under his own heartbeat.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Naruto spends the next few years carrying a message he cannot read, which is a very Itachi way to teach someone.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Now watch what happens in chapter 549, because that is where this timeline starts to unravel...

shot.fallback: hooded ninja talking to a blond boy as crows swirl around them

lines.text: Kabuto Yakushi has just raised Itachi with Edo Tensei, and he does not plan to let him think.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: He takes full control of Itachi and Nagato, then points them at the two jinchuriki.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Killer Bee faces Itachi. Naruto faces Nagato. And Itachi is not choosing a single move.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: In the real story, that control breaks in chapter 550. The crow flies out of Naruto and uses Kotoamatsukami on Itachi.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Delete that bird and the scene simply keeps going. No flash of recognition, no Itachi taking his body back.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Kabuto's hold on Edo Tensei is close to absolute. Nobody in the story has a clean way to break it from inside.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: So Itachi, one of the sharpest minds the Uchiha ever produced, becomes a weapon pointed at Killer Bee.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Bee is a veteran, but Itachi never has to hold back, because he isn't deciding anything.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: I think this is the first ripple most people miss. Naruto and Bee aren't just fighting Itachi. They're running out of options.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: They can't seal an Edo Tensei body that won't stop moving, and they can't trust the person behind it.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Think about the stakes: Kabuto isn't hunting them for sport. He wants them captured and handed over.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: So a controlled Itachi isn't a side fight. He decides whether the Allied Shinobi Forces lose both jinchuriki early.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: People say Naruto and Bee could still overpower a puppet Itachi with the Nine-Tails and the Eight-Tails together. That's the strongest counter.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: But a puppet Itachi comes with Susanoo, Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi, and none of them need a free mind to land.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Even if the jinchuriki survive, it costs chakra, time, and a Kabuto who never changes his plan.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Nagato is stuck the same way, since nobody planted a crow in him.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: So without Shisui's eye, Itachi can think, but he cannot act on a single thought.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Nothing else in the story, not Nagato's Rinnegan, not Naruto's chakra, reaches that deep.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: That's why the crow is so clever. Kotoamatsukami doesn't fight the technique. It rewrites the will the technique is holding.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Edo Tensei binds the soul to a seal, and that seal answers to Kabuto, not to who the person used to be.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Naruto can't hold back either, because Nagato keeps coming and Kabuto is watching every second.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Killer Bee is tough, but he can't talk his way past an opponent who isn't allowed to listen.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: And Itachi's Tsukuyomi is the kind of technique that ends a fight before it starts.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Every minute a puppet Itachi stays on the field is another minute the Mangekyo can be spent on Naruto's allies.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: Let me spell out the clock. Kabuto's army is already out, and the Allied Shinobi Forces are scattered.

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: And in canon, that plan has exactly one real enemy, because there is somebody Kabuto badly wants to meet next...

shot.fallback: a pale ninja with glasses controlling two reanimated warriors

lines.text: In the real story, Sasuke meets Itachi in chapter 578, and what happens next is one of the best conversations in the series.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Sasuke wants the truth from his brother, and he is willing to wait for it.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Itachi stops Sasuke from killing Kabuto, because they have to find the counter to Edo Tensei first.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Then comes Izanami, and Itachi traps Kabuto in a loop until he faces who he really is.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: That entire sequence needs one thing: Itachi's own will. No crow, no free Itachi, no Izanami.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Now picture Kabuto still holding the leash when Sasuke walks into the room.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Sasuke has already asked Itachi for the truth, and the answer is still pending.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: So he isn't facing a villain. He's facing the brother he now understands, and the brother can't say a word.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Kabuto loves that. A controlled Itachi lets him decide what the brothers say to each other, which is nothing.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Here's where I disagree with the easy answer. People say Sasuke would just take Kabuto apart on his own.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Sasuke is strong, but Kabuto in this fight has Orochimaru's cells, Sage Mode and a body that can heal.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: So Sasuke has to fight his way through a puppet army and his own brother just to reach Kabuto.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: There's a worse part. Every order Kabuto gives Itachi is one Sasuke has to answer with a blade or a retreat.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Sasuke at that stage barely trusts anyone. Watching Itachi be used again could harden him.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: This is my read: the Izanami scene isn't just a power moment. It's the place Sasuke finally gets to ask questions.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Imagine Sasuke seeing his brother's face, calm and silent, doing exactly what Kabuto wants.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: So he doesn't need Itachi to win. He only needs Itachi to hurt.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Kabuto knows how fragile Sasuke is. He studied him through Orochimaru for years.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: It's a lonelier story. And I think it's a lonelier Sasuke, which is the Sasuke Madara wants.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Take it away and the image becomes a boy facing his brother's body with no way to speak to it.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: That image is the closest the brothers ever get to the peace Itachi spent his whole life paying for.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: In canon they stand side by side, Sasuke and Itachi, and Kabuto has to face two Uchiha who finally agree.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: There's one more change here that really bothers me. The brothers never share one fight against Kabuto.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Without it, he never gets that chance, and he keeps running the same cruel experiment on everyone around him.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Lastly, think about Kabuto himself. In the real story Izanami forces him to see who he is.

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Without it, Sasuke carries every unanswered question into the final stretch of the war...

shot.fallback: two Uchiha brothers facing each other in a dim cavern

lines.text: Now the real question: what did Itachi's talk actually change?

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Before it, Sasuke was aimed at Konoha. He had decided the village's leaders should answer for what they did.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: After it, he points his anger at the war and at Madara's plan instead of the village itself.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: That is exactly the situation the crow was supposed to cover. Sasuke, Itachi's eyes, and a plan to burn Konoha down.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: In canon, the net was never used on Sasuke, because Itachi's own words reached him first.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Now look at the timeline we built. No crow means no spare Kotoamatsukami left for Sasuke either.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: So when Sasuke finally learns everything and turns toward Konoha, nothing is waiting for him.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: No bird, no brother's voice, and no promise on Naruto's side of the story.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Even Naruto's famous refusal loses something. His promise to stop Sasuke without killing him was spoken to Itachi first.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: He still keeps his bond with Sasuke, but he never carries a vow Itachi personally heard.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Does that matter? I think it does, because the vow is what kept Naruto from giving up in the darkest hours.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: And the steelman says Naruto would have acted the same either way. Maybe so. He's stubborn enough.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: But stubborn isn't the same as prepared. Itachi prepared him years before the fight.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: There's one more cost nobody mentions. Without Itachi free, there's no moment where he hands Sasuke a purpose.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Sasuke ends up fighting Kabuto, Madara and himself, with no clear idea what his brother wanted.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: That's the third consequence: a Sasuke with the truth but no blessing is the version Madara can use.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: The next time the war reaches Sasuke, Naruto is arguing with only half the story.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: He'd still fight Kabuto for Konoha. But his picture of Itachi stays the one the village told him.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Without the crow, that exchange never happens, so Naruto has no private reason to defend Itachi.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Think about what the crow scene gave them: a moment where Itachi trusted Naruto with Konoha's future.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: That's the real pivot. The war doesn't turn on a technique. It turns on which Uchiha gets to reach Sasuke first.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Sasuke would listen to the man who offers him a world where nobody can hurt his family again.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Madara's plan runs on hatred, and a Sasuke who never got his brother's last words is full of it.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Let's talk about Madara for a second, because he's the quiet winner of this timeline.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: A village that spent years fearing him now has no insurance, no truth told, and no one to speak for the Uchiha.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: It also changes how the Hokage question lands, because Konoha's future hangs on a Sasuke nobody has reached.

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: Because Madara needs a hater, and a hater with Itachi's eyes is a very sharp weapon...

shot.fallback: a lone shinobi standing at Konoha gates at dawn

lines.text: So let's put the whole chain together and see what this timeline really costs.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: One, Kabuto keeps Itachi as a living weapon, which means the jinchuriki are in far more danger.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Two, there is no Izanami and no honest conversation between the brothers.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Three, Sasuke walks toward the war with the truth and nothing to guide him.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: But here is the twist I didn't see coming the first time I traced this out.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: The crow was built to stop Sasuke from burning Konoha. Itachi planned for that, and he planned it with exactly one shot.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: In canon, that single shot was spent on Itachi himself, and I think that's the better outcome for everyone.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Only a free Itachi could talk Sasuke back from the edge. A spell could never do what his brother's words did.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: The bird didn't save Konoha by controlling the angry brother. It saved Konoha by setting the loving one free.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Take that one trust away and the rest of the dominoes fall one by one toward Kabuto.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: It mattered because Itachi trusted Naruto, and Naruto trusted a stranger enough to carry the bird.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: So when you ask whether the crow mattered, the answer is yes, but not the way the plan said.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: That's the part that gets me. The cleverest piece of the plan worked on the one person Itachi never aimed it at.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: So the best day for that crow is the day it is never used on its target.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: If Sasuke had needed the genjutsu, it would have meant Itachi's words had already failed him.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Itachi's most carefully built fail-safe pays off by missing its original target.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: Add it up and I think you land on something uncomfortable for fans of the original plan.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: One small bird opened the only door through which Itachi could speak to his brother again.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: That's my answer to the question I opened with. The crow wasn't a weapon, it was a door.

shot.fallback: hooded ninja with a crow on his shoulder walking away

lines.text: And if you want to see the man who gave up that eye in the first place, Shisui's story is the next video.
